title: Mammogram
what: An X-ray of the breasts. Each breast is pressed between plates for a few seconds so the picture is clear.
why: To find breast cancer early, usually every 1 to 2 years after age 40 to 50, or if you feel a lump.
tell_doctor: If you are pregnant or breastfeeding
If you have had breast surgery
If you have felt a lump, and exactly where

prepare.title: Time in your cycle
prepare.text: Days 5 to 12 of your cycle are best, when your breasts are less tender. If you have no periods, any day is fine.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: On the day of the test, do not put deodorant, lotion, or powder on your breasts or underarms. They show up as spots on the image.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear a skirt or trousers with a top, so you only undress to the waist.

bring: Past mammograms and breast ultrasounds. Comparing them is very important
steps: You undress to the waist and stand at the machine
The technician places one breast on a platform
A plate comes down and presses the breast for a few seconds
An image is taken, then another angle and the other breast. Usually 4 images
feel: The pressure is unpleasant, sometimes painful, but only for a few seconds
Tell the technician if it hurts a lot
after: The report usually comes within 1 to 3 days
Sometimes you are called back for an extra image or an ultrasound. This is common and no reason to panic

faq.q: Why is the breast pressed so hard?
faq.a: It spreads the tissue evenly, makes the image clearer, and lowers the radiation dose.
They are different tests. A mammogram is usually done after 40. Ultrasound is for younger women and as an extra test. The doctor decides.

reminders.text: Mammogram tomorrow. In the morning, do not put deodorant or lotion on your breasts or underarms.
